title: One-Roll Temple — Particular Quirks About the Temple

entries.value: It is built into a former secular building — a Roman bath, a great hall
It is remarkably well-fortified for a religious house
It is connected to a thriving secular business — a mill, a farm, a workshop
The clergy are largely related to each other by blood
It is in an unusually dangerous location — a cliff, a flood-plain, a moor
It shares its precinct with a friendly but different faith
It follows unusual prohibitions or practises rites not found elsewhere
It has access to an ancient relic or holy object of real power
Its library or archive is remarkably extensive
It attracts wandering prophets, mystics, and religious merchants
It provides some service that polite society finds illicit or scandalous
It is more a business or farm than a genuine religious house
It is unusually beautifully built or decorated
It is a shadow of a once-glorious past — crumbling, underpopulated
It is unusually recent in its founding — within living memory
The clergy generally dislike each other intensely
Its leadership is of foreign origin or background
It deals only with those who have proven their faith
It displaced a former faith, perhaps violently
It is secretly a front for another faith entirely
